unmapped: Reward is the product (AND) of independent Bernoulli item weights over the chosen ordered tuple (conjunctive, non-linear reward); a disjunctive (OR) variant is also covered
Feedback is the index of the first chosen item with weight zero (cascade feedback over arbitrary feasible tuples)
Item weights are independent across items (factored distribution)
settings.definition_quote: A combinatorial cascading bandit is a tuple $B = (E, P, \Theta)$ ... receives a binary reward $\rnd{r}_t = \min_{e \in \rnd{A}_t} \rnd{w}_t(e)$ ... the agent observes the index of the first item in $\rnd{A}_t$ whose weight is zero ... the distribution $P$ is factored ... $P_e$ is a Bernoulli distribution with mean $\bar{w}(e)$.

symbols.m: paper's K: maximum number of items in any feasible solution
symbols.f_star: expected reward of the optimal solution, f(A*, w_bar) > 0
symbols.Delta_e_min: minimum gap of suboptimal item e: f* minus max reward of suboptimal solutions containing e
symbols.sum_subopt: here: sum over suboptimal items e not in A*

conditions: optimal solution A* unique as a set
algorithm initialized with one sample w_0 ~ P

source.label: thm:ucb1
source.quote: The regret of $\combcascade$ is bounded as $\displaystyle R(n) \leq \frac{K}{f^\ast} \sum_{e \in \tilde{E}} \frac{4272}{\Delta_{e, \min}} \log n + \frac{\pi^2}{3} L$.

results.notes: Regret R(n)=E[sum f(A*,w_t)-f(A_t,w_t)] equals expected gap sum, hence pseudo-regret. Same bound holds for the disjunctive variant with Delta_e_min and f* redefined via 1-w_bar. Computationally efficient given a linear optimization oracle on Theta.

source.label: thm:gap-free
source.quote: The regret of $\combcascade$ is bounded as $\displaystyle R(n) \leq 131 \sqrt{\frac{K L n \log n}{f^\ast}} + \frac{\pi^2}{3} L$.

results.notes: epsilon is chosen only in the analysis, the algorithm does not need n. Depends on f*, so not purely worst case. Also applies to the disjunctive variant.
